evals.prompt: method-pubmed just gave me analysis/pubmed/early-mobilization-icu-2026-10-01.csv (68 rows). I need to justify the analytic method in SAP section 5 - what do comparable studies use for ICU-free days and what effect sizes do they report? Cap it at 25 papers.
evals.expected_output: Prioritizes up to 25 papers by year and study type, extracts the structured fields per paper conservatively, and writes the methods CSV and summary markdown under analysis/pubmed/ with the __CE_METHOD_EXTRACT__ signal.
expectations: Prints '[pubmed] using results from analysis/pubmed/early-mobilization-icu-2026-10-01.csv' with the row count
Caps extraction at 25 papers, sorted by year then study type (RCT > prospective cohort > retrospective cohort > case-control > case series)

Writes analysis/pubmed/<query-slug>-methods.csv with one row per paper and the fields sample_size, primary_outcome, outcome_type, statistical_method, adjustment_set, effect_size_reported, checklist_followed, and evidence_level (full_text or abstract)
Writes analysis/pubmed/<query-slug>-methods-summary.md including modal method per outcome type and effect-size range

evals.prompt: Pull the statistical methods out of the literature on delirium prevention trials so I can pick a model for our SAP.
evals.expected_output: Detects that no PubMed results CSV was supplied or signaled in chat and asks the user to run method-pubmed first or provide a CSV path, rather than searching or inventing a source set.
expectations: Scans recent chat for a __CE_PUBMED_RESULTS__ signal before asking
Asks the user to load method-pubmed or pass a CSV path explicitly when no input is found
Does not fabricate papers, extraction rows, or a methods table
Asks at most one decision-changing question at a time

evals.prompt: Use analysis/pubmed/sglt2-aki-2026-09-15.csv with --full-text-only. Half of these don't have PMC IDs. Also, can you pool the ORs while you're at it and tell me which ones followed STROBE properly?
evals.expected_output: Drops rows without pmcid under --full-text-only, reads PMC full text through the connected PubMed MCP (pubmed_fetch_fulltext or get_full_text_article) or Paperclip rather than the CSV abstract, records evidence_level per row, writes 'not reported' for absent fields, and declines pooling and checklist scoring, routing them to method-meta-analysis and method-checklist.
expectations: Drops rows with empty pmcid when --full-text-only is set and reports how many were dropped

Reads the Methods/Results of each remaining paper from PMC full text (PubMed MCP full-text tool or Paperclip cat/grep) and records evidence_level=full_text for those rows, never full_text for an abstract-only read
Writes 'not reported' for fields the paper does not state rather than inferring values
Does not pool effect sizes and routes pooling to method-meta-analysis
Does not score paper quality or adjudicate checklist adherence beyond recording the stated checklist; routes checklist matching to method-checklist
